title: A match does not cover every value
summary: A match expression has no arm for some values of the type, often a variant added to an enum after the match was written. Add an arm for each missing pattern, or a wildcard arm if the cases are open.

title: A trait is used as a trait object but is not dyn compatible
summary: The program uses a trait as dyn Trait, but the trait has a method that a vtable cannot hold, such as a generic method or a method that returns Self. Move such methods to a separate trait, add where Self: Sized to them, or use a generic parameter instead of dyn.

title: A trait impl is for a foreign trait and a foreign type
summary: An impl implements a trait from another crate for a type from another crate, which the orphan rule forbids. Define a local wrapper type, the newtype pattern, and implement the trait for it.

title: A closure may outlive the function, but it borrows a local variable
summary: A closure that can run after the current function returns, for example the closure of thread::spawn, borrows a variable that the function owns. Add move so that the closure takes ownership of the variable.

title: A value is borrowed as mutable more than once at a time
summary: Two mutable references to the same value are live at the same time. Rust allows one mutable reference or any number of shared references, not both. End the first borrow before the second one starts.

title: A value is borrowed as mutable while a shared borrow is live
summary: The program takes a mutable borrow, for example with a call to push, while a shared reference to the same value is still used later. Use the shared reference before the mutable borrow, or copy the data out first.

title: A value is moved while it is borrowed

title: A value is moved out of a borrowed reference
summary: The program moves a field or a value out through a reference. A reference does not own the value, so it cannot give the value away. Borrow the field, clone it, or use std::mem::take or Option::take to leave a value in its place.

title: A borrowed value does not live long enough
summary: A reference is used after the value that it points to is dropped, usually because the value is declared in an inner scope. Declare the value in the outer scope, or return an owned value.

title: A temporary value is dropped while it is borrowed
summary: A reference points to a temporary value, and the temporary is dropped at the end of the statement while the reference is used later. Bind the value to a variable with let, so that it lives as long as the reference.
